in_urdu.name: عصر
in_urdu.long_meaning: عصر نام ہے جس کا تعلق زمان سے ہے، یہ نام قرآن میں بھی موجود ہے، اس کا مطلب ہے وقت یا فترة، یا اس وقت کا نام جب کبھی کوئی چیز شروع ہوتی ہے، یہ نام مسلمانوں میں بہت مقبول ہے، اس وقت کے نسل کی اولاد کو عرف عام میں اس کے نام سے پکایا جاتا ہے

data.cultural_impact: The name "Asr" comes from the Arabic word for "afternoon" or "the later part of the day." In Islamic culture, this time between the Zuhr (midday) and Asr (afternoon) prayer holds significant importance. This period is often used for rest and relaxation, as many businesses close during this time for the afternoon prayer. In some Islamic communities, there are also traditional customs and practices associated with Asr, such as taking a siesta or engaging in educational activities.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Asr is a time of reflection and contemplation for Muslims. It is one of the five daily prayers, and the act of performing Asr prayer reminds Muslims of their commitment to Allah and the importance of striving for spiritual growth and purity of heart. During the time between the Zuhr and Asr prayers, Muslims are encouraged to seek Allah's forgiveness, ask for guidance, and offer thanks for His blessings. Asr is also believed to be the time when the gates of paradise are closest to the earth, offering an additional spiritual incentive for Muslims to make the most of this time for prayer and devotion.

historical_references.context: The Battle of Ain Jalut: Salahuddin Ayyubi's victory against the Mongols in 638 AH (1241 AD) led to the establishment of the Mamluk Sultanate. The Mamluks, under their sultan Qutuz, defeated the Mongols once again in 658 AH (1260 AD) during the Battle of Ain Jalut. The prayer time of Asr was established and recognized as the fourth prayer of the day during the rule of Sultan Qutuz.

historical_references.context: During the reign of Sultan Al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qitbay, the prayer time of Asr was moved from its original position after the Dhuhr prayer due to the change in solar position. This shift was confirmed by Fakhr al-Din al-Razi and other scholars of the time.
